dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality. When did you first notice the swelling in your neck?
I first noticed it about two months ago. It's been slowly getting bigger since then, but it doesn't hurt or anything like that.
I see. Have you noticed any other symptoms like difficulty swallowing, changes in your voice, or unexplained weight loss?
No, I haven't had any trouble swallowing or changes in my voice. My weight has been pretty stable too.
I understand. Where exactly on your neck is the swelling located, and is it right in the middle or off to one side?
It's on the back of my neck, right at the nape. It's pretty much in the middle, not really off to either side.
When you touch the swelling, does it feel soft and doughy, or is it firm and hard? Does it move around easily under the skin if you press on it?
It feels pretty firm, not really soft or squishy. And yeah, it does seem to move a little bit when I press on it, but not a whole lot.

Does the skin over the swelling look normal, or have you noticed any redness or a small opening in the center? I would also like to perform a physical examination to better assess the lump. REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination

RESULTS: Physical examination reveals:

**Vital Signs:**
- Temperature: 37.3°C (99.1°F)
- Blood Pressure: 130/86 mm Hg
- Heart Rate: 88/min
- Respiratory Rate: Normal

**Neck Examination:**
- A 2.5-cm (1-inch) firm, mobile, painless nodule located on the nape of the neck
- Notable finding: The skin over the nodule cannot be pinched (suggesting the lesion is attached to the overlying skin)
- No lymphadenopathy or thyromegaly detected

**Lung Examination:**
- Clear breath sounds bilaterally
- No rales, rhonchi, or wheezes

**Remainder of Examination:**
- No other abnormalities detected

Have you ever noticed any discharge or a small opening, like a blackhead, on the surface of the lump? I would also like to get an ultrasound to see the internal structure of the nodule more clearly. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Neck

RESULTS: 

**Ultrasound of the Neck:**
- Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature
Since the ultrasound shows a cystic nature and the skin is attached, have you ever noticed a tiny dark spot or any thick, smelly drainage coming from the lump? I would also like to know
No, I haven't seen any dark spot or opening on it. And there's definitely been no drainage or any kind of smell coming from it at all.

Thank you for that information. Have you noticed any other similar lumps on your scalp or other parts of your body? I would also like to perform a fine needle aspiration to examine the contents of the
No, I haven't noticed any other lumps anywhere else on my body. And sure, if you think the needle aspiration will help figure out what this is, I'm okay with that.
I'll proceed with the fine needle aspiration now to examine the contents of the nodule. Has anyone in your family ever had similar recurring skin cysts or lumps? REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle

RESULTS: The requested test "Fine_Needle" aspiration is not available in the current data. However, based on the available information, all other test results show NORMAL READINGS for complete blood count (WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets normal) and serum chemistry (Creatinine and Liver Enzymes normal), with the exception of elevated glucose levels.

The physical examination and ultrasound findings as previously reported show:
- A well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the subcutaneous tissue
- 2.5-cm firm, mobile nodule with skin attachment
- No signs of infection or inflammation

Fine needle aspiration results are not currently available in the system.
I see. Since the ultrasound confirms it is a cystic lesion attached to the skin, I'll request a biopsy to get a definitive diagnosis. Has the lump ever become inflamed, red, or painful since
No, it's never gotten red or inflamed, and like I mentioned before, it hasn't been painful at all. It's just been sitting there getting slowly bigger over the past couple months.
I understand that it hasn't been painful or inflamed. Since the lump is firm and attached to the skin, I'd like to perform an excisional biopsy to confirm its nature and provide
Okay, that sounds reasonable. If you think removing it and testing it is the best way to figure out what it is, I'm willing to go ahead with that.
I'll perform the excisional biopsy now to get a definitive answer. While we wait for those results, have you ever had any trauma or injury to that area of your neck
No, I can't recall any injury or trauma to that area. I do play golf pretty regularly, but I haven't hit my neck or anything like that.
That's good to know, and it helps rule out a few possibilities. I would now like to review the results from the excisional biopsy to get a definitive look at the tissue. REQUEST TEST:

**Available Test Results:**

The excisional biopsy results are not currently available in the system and would need to be performed and processed to obtain definitive histopathological diagnosis.
Since the biopsy results aren't available yet, I'd like to ask if the area over the lump has hair and if you've noticed any hair loss there. This can help distinguish between
Yes, there is hair over that area, and no, I haven't noticed any hair loss there. The hair seems pretty normal as far as I can tell.
That is helpful to know. Have you noticed if the lump feels particularly smooth and spherical, almost like a small marble under the skin? I'll also check if it seems to be getting firmer over

It does feel pretty smooth and round, kind of like what you're describing. As for getting firmer, I'm not really sure - it's been firm since I first noticed it, so I can't say if it's changed much in that way.
That is very helpful to know. Since the nodule is firm and attached to the skin but has no visible opening, I'd like to ask if you've noticed it getting any larger specifically after
I'm not sure what you mean by "after" - after what? It's just been gradually getting bigger over the past two months, pretty steadily as far as I can tell.

My apologies for the confusion, I was wondering if you noticed any changes after physical activity like golfing. Given the firm, smooth, and mobile nature of this cyst at the nape of your neck and the lack
No, I haven't noticed it changing with activity or after I play golf. It just seems to stay the same size and feel, whether I'm active or resting.
I understand. Since the lump is smooth and firm but has no visible opening, has anyone in your family ever had similar cysts on their scalp or neck? This information helps me confirm if this might be
No, I don't think anyone in my family has had anything like this. At least not that I'm aware of or that anyone's ever mentioned to me.
Thank you for confirming that. Given the firm, marble-like feel of the nodule and its location at the nape of your neck, does the lump feel like it's deeply seated
No, it doesn't feel really deep - it seems to be just under the skin, not way down in there. I can feel it pretty easily when I touch the back of my neck.
